brueghel-sight.label: Collaborative allegorical picture-gallery scene
brueghel-sight.reason: The curator-authored series entry distinguishes Rubens's figure contribution from Brueghel's elaborate settings and identifies actual pictures represented within Sight. This supports a contextual label for a painting about looking and collecting, not a presumed response from a visitor.

documentedContext.claim: The curator identifies Rubens as the maker of the main personifications and Brueghel as the maker of their settings. Some small represented paintings refer to actual works, including their collaborative Madonna and Child in a Garland of Flowers.

friedrich-moonrise.label: Romantic evening landscape with back-turned figures
friedrich-moonrise.reason: The official anniversary project identifies the painting as the evening counterpart to The Solitary Tree and describes the three seated figures, ships and moon. This is an object-specific pairing and arrangement, not a universal meaning of a moonlit sea.

documentedContext.claim: The painting was commissioned as the evening counterpart to The Solitary Tree. The published commission account records that both works were completed by November1822.

gauguin-call.label: Late imagined figural scene
gauguin-call.reason: The exact CMA record describes the quiet beckoning gesture as an ambiguous event and places the object among Gauguin's late works about life and death. This contextual description does not establish the subject's emotion or a viewer's beliefs.

documentedContext.claim: CMA presents the beckoning gesture as unresolved and connects this work with a late group exploring life and death. Its interpretation is kept separate from the visibly quiet bodily action.

teotihuacan-mural.label: Classic-period Teotihuacán processional mural fragment
teotihuacan-mural.reason: The API identifies this as a fresco wall fragment in Teotihuacán style and qualifies the possible compound attribution. The object's fragmentary format is retained; no complete wall scheme is reconstructed from it.

documentedContext.claim: CMA identifies the figure as part of a repeated procession and reads the mouth scroll as materialised chant or prayer. The museum's possible associations of the maguey spines remain qualified interpretations.

add-mondrian-composition-1930.label: Neoplasticism with displaced rectangular divisions
add-mondrian-composition-1930.reason: Kunsthaus Zürich's exact object commentary calls Mondrian's method Neoplasticism and describes this composition's large red field, peripheral black bars and smaller blue/yellow areas. This is distinct from treating all geometric abstraction as one handling or composition.

documentedContext.claim: Kunsthaus Zürich relates the painting's vertical and horizontal divisions and primary colours to Mondrian's Neoplasticism. The record describes a type developed around1930 rather than assigning every Mondrian the same layout.

tanner-waters.label: Religious etching with later publication credit

add-malevich-football-player.label: Early Suprematist nonfigurative painting
add-malevich-football-player.reason: The Art Institute's exact object commentary identifies this as one of the first Suprematist paintings and warns that its descriptive title does not tell the viewer which represented natural form to find. documentedContext.claim: The Art Institute places this object in the first group of Suprematist works and explains that the fourth-dimension wording refers to a mathematical idea used by artists. The title is context rather than evidence of a visibly depicted footballer.

piazza-san-marco.label: Attributed Venetian veduta
piazza-san-marco.reason: The museum creator entry explicitly says attributed to Bernardo Bellotto. The detailed named architecture supports a Venetian city-view label; attribution uncertainty is retained and the depicted city is not automatically the place of execution.
